description.value: The Bell that Failed: Objective: find the missing dawn voice. Search the levy chest or win the keeper's testimony; delay costs tenant seed.
Names at the Threshold: Objective: contact the erased children. Learn their signs or follow reflected marks; delay isolates one child.
The Penance Gate: Objective: admit the sick safely. Challenge the token rule or escort the hospice route; delay exhausts a patient.
Grain under Guard: Objective: recover shared reserves. Prove the false defense order or negotiate witnessed release; delay empties tenant stores.
The House's Own Debt: Objective: identify who broke the pact. Read the registry or protect the heir's testimony; delay burns the ledger.
Smoke in the Hospice: Objective: separate disease from imposed harm. Test the censer or compare recovery records; delay creates false cases.
Fields beyond the Oath: Objective: protect unsworn farmers. Repair a patrol route or draw the hounds away; delay destroys the next harvest.
The Mirror Nursery: Objective: keep children's memories intact. Share spoken signs or isolate the leech; delay erases a bond.
A Saint who Must Sleep: Objective: protect the bearer's agency. Form a care rotation or enforce a rest charter; delay prevents another safe dose.
The First Contract: Objective: establish universal protection. Recover the archive or call contract witnesses; delay strengthens the captain's claim.
Three Houses at the River: Objective: renew names without ransom. Convene shared witnesses or restore the older verse; delay divides the children.
Water before Confession: Objective: produce a safe shared cure. Test diluted doses or clean the well; delay feeds the counterfeit market.
A Defense Worth Paying: Objective: set a fair levy. Compare patrol needs or accept bounded repair obligations; delay leaves a gate undefended.
A Name of One's Own: Objective: give children control of identity. Create an unowned register or witness individual names; delay replaces the old debt.
The Queue by Need: Objective: allocate treatment fairly. Use hospice triage or a rotating public list; delay harms the weakest patients.
Dawn for Everyone: Objective: settle field protection. Fund common defense or a witnessed tenant covenant; record who controls the bell.
The Released Pact: Objective: end inherited naming ransom. Dissolve the house claim or bind accountable witnesses; record children's chosen terms.
The Bearer's Road: Objective: settle the cure agreement. Share dosage knowledge or maintain voluntary rotating care; record the bearer's right to leave.
Silent Dawn: the bell fails while levy soldiers demand fresh oaths.
Forgotten Child: a mother cannot read the name she wrote moments earlier.
Denied Ration: the marshal turns away a feverish traveler without a penance token.
Seed Seizure: the captain orders tenant grain moved into his chest.
Heir Recognition: an erased child recognizes the witch's heir from the old nursery.
Unconfessed Recovery: a patient improves after clean water and rest.
Warning Rhythm: the cracked bell attracts hounds rather than driving them away.
Nursery Message: children communicate through mirror signs the court cannot erase.
Bearer Exhaustion: Oren collapses after a forced public cure.
Contract Found: the universal protection clause appears in a funeral archive.
Registry Lock: the bailiff seals records before the children can testify.
Smoke Diagnosis: the censer's irritant is identified as a source of false symptoms.
Tenant Assembly: farmers offer repair labor if levy rules are made public.
House Threat: Tessa threatens a new curse if her broken promise is exposed.
Rest Refusal: the jailer blocks a care rotation and calls it desertion.
Field Decoy: a lantern route can draw the hounds away at the price of a watch crew.
Old Verse: Kira recalls a naming formula accountable to shared witnesses.
Dose Trial: a diluted cure works when the well water is clean.
Clapper Return: the keeper reveals where the captain hid the bell's voice.
Mirror Breach: a leech enters the nursery through an isolated child's reflection.
Food Hearing: the kitchen demands that treatment and hunger be separated from guilt.
Gate Repair: freeholders must choose a defense schedule before the dusk swarm returns.
Heir Confession: Mei offers testimony with a promise that no child replaces her debt.
Bearer Petition: Oren asks for the right to travel after the cure is shared.
Oath Reckoning: the captain offers defense in exchange for permanent grain control.
Names Spoken: the children can decide who witnesses their restored identities.
Cure Queue: the hospice chooses priority by need rather than token ownership.
Dawn for Tenants: the bell's new schedule reflects the final protection agreement.
Pact Released: the register changes according to the children's chosen terms.
Pilgrimage Ends: the bearer leaves or stays under an agreement he helped write.
